newsitem.title: ZAIRE: UNHCR repatriates more Rwandan refugees from Zaire.
newsitem.headline: UNHCR repatriates more Rwandan refugees from Zaire.

text.p: The U.N. refugee agency UNHCR flew more than 660 Rwandan refugees home from Kisangani in northeastern Zaire on Friday, bringing the total since the airlift began on Sunday to almost 2,500, a UNHCR spokesman said.
The refugees, members of Rwanda's Hutu majority, fled their homeland in 1994 and the country's minority Tutsis collectively accuse them of genocide in Rwanda the same year.
Many abandoned their camps south of Kisangani last week after attacks by villagers and Zairean Tutsi-dominated rebels but this week the refugees have been emerging from forests.
Paul Stromberg, UNHCR spokesman in the northeast Zairean city of Kisangani, told Reuters two flights left Kisangani early on Friday and at least three would follow later in the day.
"That includes a medical evacuation of serious cases to Gisenyi (in Rwanda)...That could be 30 to 40 people," he added.

He said UNHCR had only 1,450 refugees left at a transit site in Kisangani awaiting repatriation but trains would bring more from Biaro camp, 41 km (25 miles) south of Kisangani. About 30,000 Rwandans have returned to Biaro camp and want to go to Rwanda, he added.
